newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bourse drops in relatively light trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bourse drops in relatively light trade.

text.p: The Irish bourse on Monday shaved almost two percentage points off the index but turnover was relatively light and focus remained on Wall Street, dealers said.
"Wall Street has not shown any strong direction so far and we have seen stocks come off but volumes are very thin," one equity dealer said.

Both the UK's FTSE 100 index and Wall Street were showing muted activity, with the FTSE closing 0.6 pct lower and the Dow, which shed more than three percent on Friday, was up 0.46 points at 7,695 by 1601 GMT.
The ISEQ index of shares dropped 71.82 points to 3,584.15.
Financial stocks continued to slide in the domestic market with Bank of Ireland down 12 pence and AIB off eight pence at 790 and 585 pence respectively.
In the industrial sector, CHR shed 11 pence to 726, while Smurfit dropped six pence to 225 pence.

"We are taking our lead from Wall Street and the trend seems to be that when Wall Street plunges one day it tends to recoup most of its losses the next day," the dealer said. "But still it is anyones guess where it will be by the close."
